title: Slope-weighted cost distance for modeling flood dynamics: a physics-informed random forest approach
abstract: Rapid flood inundation forecasting is a crucial tool for disaster mitigation; however, physically-based models are computationally intensive, and conventional data-driven models often exhibit poor generalizability and limited interpretability. To address these deficiencies, we propose a novel physics-informed random forest framework that incorporates a slope-weighted cost-distance feature to represent spatiotemporal flood dynamics and validate the framework using data from the Kinugawa River Basin, Japan. By weighting the distance with the terrain gradient, this feature approximates gravity-driven flow paths, enabling the model to significantly outperform the static baselines (F1-score improvement from 0.507 to 0.893). To improve performance for hydrographs withheld from training but drawn from the predefined 31-scenario set, we introduced a hydrograph feature-space sampling strategy. The strategy selects representative training cases by clustering peak discharge and total volume; using only four training cases, it achieved an F1-score of 0.904 for the withheld scenarios. Furthermore, a SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis provided quantitative evidence that the model learned statistical relationships consistent with flow-path selection and volume-related flood expansion. The proposed framework offers a transparent and computationally efficient alternative to black-box deep learning models for real-time forecasting, while its reliability for hydrographs beyond the sampled discharge-volume and waveform range remains untested

title: Learning water diversion behaviour in regulated river networks using graph neural networks and neural decision trees
abstract: Human water diversions alter river dynamics and are difficult to represent when operational rules are uncertain or discontinuous. This study investigates how graph-based deep learning models represent diversion behaviour in river networks under varying degrees of prior operational knowledge. Using SWAT+ simulations as an internally consistent synthetic benchmark, we design controlled diversion scenarios of increasing rule complexity. We compare graph attention networks that embed river network topology and diversion connectivity directly into their model structure, with no prior operational information, with partial structural constraints, with fully prescribed rules applied in post-processing, and with a hybrid architecture that explicitly separates hydrological prediction from operational decision-making via a Neural Decision Tree. All approaches reproduce total flow before diversion robustly, while diverted flow skill declines with operational complexity. Additional operational knowledge does not consistently improve predictive accuracy, as diversion errors are dominated by propagation from total-flow uncertainty. The hybrid model achieves comparable skill while providing explicit and analysable decision representations, highlighting trade-offs between flexibility, robustness, and interpretability. The modular and structurally explicit formulation illustrates how graph-based AI components can support transparent and interpretable representations of operational decision-making in regulated river systems, though validation across diverse catchments and real-world operational conditions remains necessary.

title: Physics-guided symbolic regression of nonlocal transport memory from sparse observations in aquatic systems
abstract: Predicting non-Fickian transport in aquatic systems from sparse observations is challenging because historical effects and spatial heterogeneity often control present behavior. We introduce a physics-guided, sequential hybrid framework that couples nonlocal transport theory with deep-learning-assisted symbolic regression to infer transport memory directly from one-dimensional observations, such as breakthrough curves (BTCs) or spatial concentration snapshots. The physics module maps observations to a nonparametric memory representation derived from the statistics of microscopic particle dynamics, including temporal memory associated with mass-transfer-controlled transport and spatial (kinematic) memory represented by the streamtube velocity probability density function (PDF) for conductivity-driven spreading, thereby unifying temporal and spatial nonlocality within a single construct. Neural reconstruction, coupled with a stable numerical Laplace transform, produces denoised, high-resolution spectral representations, from which symbolic regression identifies compact, closed-form expressions for transport memory that are embedded back into the nonlocal model. Validation spans synthetic and experimental systems: semi-analytical fractional diffusion and a Cr(VI) column experiment (power-law kernels); a Red Cedar River tracer test (reach-specific, exponentially tempered kernels); random-walk particle tracking (Gamma-family velocity laws); groundwater tracer transport at the MADE field site (independently referred inverse-Gamma velocity PDFs for MADE-1 and MADE-2 with out-of-sample predictive skill); and sediment transport in the North Loup River (a symmetric heavy-tailed velocity PDF capturing both backward and forward scaling). Across all cases, the inferred models reproduce observed transport behavior and accurately predict withheld profiles while remaining interpretable and parsimonious, without requiring prior characterization of aquatic system properties beyond geometry and boundary conditions. Compared to a purely data-driven sparse-regression approach on the same MADE-2 dataset, which yields only a near-integer-order advection equation (\alpha = 0.99​) with no dispersion, our physics-guided framework captures the anomalous spreading and predicts withheld concentration snapshots, demonstrating enhanced robustness under sparse, noisy conditions. By bridging data-driven inference with nonlocal transport physics and expanding the concept of transport memory to encompass both temporal and spatial nonlocality, the proposed framework provides a practical and interpretable pathway for modeling anomalous transport under observational constraints common in laboratory and field hydrologic systems. This capability enables practical inference of dominant transport mechanisms and plume evolution in field systems where only sparse monitoring data are available.

title: Grounding large language models in hydrologic modelling
abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) possess extensive hydrological knowledge, they often struggle to appropriately simulate complex physical processes in hydrological systems. To address this limitation, we present an LLM-based agentic intelligent modelling approach for hydrological time-series forecasting (HydroAIM). HydroAIM decouples the multi-agent architecture through the model context protocol (MCP) to integrate an expert task workflow, a standardised algorithmic workflow (SAW) library, and an iterative feedback closed-loop execution toolbox. Comprehensive experiments demonstrated that across 100 modelling tasks of varying types utilising four LLMs, HydroAIM achieved an execution success rate of 91%. Ablation studies have revealed that removing the expert task workflow causes complete system failure owing to planning chaos, plummeting the success rate to 0%. This result indicates that long-horizon task planning is the core bottleneck restricting LLMs from executing hydrological modelling tasks. Furthermore, when applied to 671 catchments in the Catchment Attributes and Meteorology for Large-sample Studies (CAMELS) dataset without human intervention, HydroAIM achieves median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) values of 0.63 and 0.64 for local and global modelling, respectively, meeting the application benchmarks established by traditional physical models. This study not only demonstrates the capability of LLMs as a hydrologic modelling tool but also provides a scalable pathway for grounding general LLMs in quantitative tasks within specialised scientific domains.

title: Ensembling or not? On the value of boosting and bagging for physics-aware machine learning in hydrology
abstract: • Ensembling adds limited value to physics-aware Machine Learning (PaML) models. • Single well-configured PaML matches ensemble performance • Classical boosting compensates low-capacity PaML learners. • Bagging provides limited additional predictive benefit. • GrowNet-inspired boosting shows non-monotonic behavior. Ensemble machine learning methods such as bagging and boosting are widely used to improve predictive performance in hydrological modeling. However, their value when applied to physics-aware machine learning (PaML) models remains largely unexplored. This study investigates whether ensemble strategies provide tangible predictive gains over a standalone PaML model for streamflow simulation. Four controlled experiments were conducted on five representative catchments from the Catchment Attributes and Meteorology for Large-sample Studies dataset for the contiguous United States (CAMELS-US) to evaluate the influence of training epochs, base learner capacity, ensemble size, and training data length. Bagging, classical boosting, and a growth-based boosting formulation inspired by GrowNet were compared against both weak and well-configured single PaML models. Predictive performance was assessed using the Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE), the Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGE) and the normalized root mean square error (NRMSE). Results show that ensemble strategies do not yield substantial improvements over a properly configured standalone PaML model, despite requiring greater computational resources. While classical boosting can compensate for intentionally reduced model capacity by aggregating low-capacity PaML learners, the resulting gains remain marginal relative to a moderately expressive single model. Bagging provides limited additional benefits, and the growth-based boosting formulation exhibits non-monotonic and basin-dependent behavior. Overall, the findings suggest that, within the investigated framework, refining the architecture and capacity of a single PaML model is generally more effective than adopting ensemble strategies. These results contribute to clarifying the practical role of ensemble learning in physics-aware hydrological modeling.

title: Regional landslide early warning through machine-learning-based rainfall threshold and hydromorphological slope units
abstract: Regional landslide early warning (LEW) remains a fundamental challenge because of the spatial heterogeneity of hydrological–geomorphological units and the nonlinear responses inherent in rainfall-triggering processes. This study develops an integrated LEW framework that combines landslide susceptibility prediction (LSP) with rainfall-threshold modeling based on machine learning (ML) to advance the quantitative characterization of regional-scale rainfall-landslide hydrology. For spatial characterization, we propose a novel LSP model that integrates hydrological analysis (HA) and multi-scale segmentation (MSS) to better represent hydromorphological controls on the spatial distribution of slope failures. The HA–MSS model demonstrates strong spatial discriminability: “very high susceptibility” zones capture 69.33 % of observed landslides while occupying only 6.76 % of the total area. For temporal prediction, an ML-based rainfall-threshold model trained jointly on triggering and non-triggering events achieves a probability of detection of 0.82, an accuracy of 0.85, a probability of false detection of 0.13, and a Hanssen–Kuipers index of 0.69, substantially outperforming the empirical E–D baseline. Feature-importance analysis identifies event cumulative rainfall (ECR), maximum intensity (Imax), intensity (I), and duration (D) as dominant predictors, whereas antecedent rainfall variables (AR3, AR5, AR7) contribute 35.2 % of the total feature importance, highlighting the importance of antecedent wetness conditions in rainfall-induced landslide triggering. The integrated framework supports dynamic warning updates at hourly resolution through a spatiotemporal warning matrix. Retrospective assessment of the integrated LEW showed that approximately 87 % of historical landslides were associated with red or orange alert levels, while the August 2021 hindcast reproduced the temporal escalation and spatial evolution of warning levels during an intense rainfall event.

title: Improving flood forecasts: the combined impact of data assimilation and machine learning post-processing
abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasts are essential for flood risk management and impact mitigation. Coupling hydrological models with machine learning techniques has gained increasing attention as a means to improve forecast skill, with post-processing emerging as a promising approach to correcting systematic model residuals. However, the interaction between machine-learning post-processing, data assimilation and calibration strategies remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we assess the contribution of machine-learning-based post-processing to hourly streamflow forecasts for 687 catchments in metropolitan France, generated using a GR-family hydrological model (GR5H-RI) under three forecasting approaches differing in calibration strategy and use of data assimilation. Random Forest and Multilayer Perceptron models are used to post-process forecasts at lead times of 3, 6, 12 and 24 h. Forecast performance is evaluated using both continuous skill metrics relative to persistence and threshold-based metrics for flood event detection. Results show that (1) post-processing consistently improves forecast skill at short lead times, especially for slower-response catchments, with the median persistence score increasing from 0.33 to 0.54 at a 3-h lead time in the highest-skill forecasting setup and performance improving in 89.7% of catchments; (2) the largest gains occur for forecasts without data assimilation, suggesting that post-processing can partially compensate for the lack of state updating but cannot fully replace it; and (3) neural network-based post-processing slightly outperforms tree-based models in continuous metrics, while differences are more limited for event detection. Overall, results highlight the complementary roles of data assimilation and machine-learning post-processing and demonstrate the potential of such frameworks for operational flood forecasting.

title: Toward AI-driven digital twins for metropolitan floods: A conditional latent dynamics network surrogate of the shallow water equations
abstract: AI-driven flood digital twins demand fast hydrodynamic surrogates for ensemble forecasting and observation assimilation. Yet even GPU-accelerated two-dimensional shallow water equation (SWE) solvers still require minutes per -hour run on a -million-active-cell metropolitan basin (the Des Plaines River basin at resolution), making such workloads prohibitive at native resolution. We present the Conditional Latent Dynamics Network (CLDNet): a low-dimensional latent neural ODE driven by rainfall, paired with a coordinate-based decoder conditioned on static terrain (elevation, slope, Manning roughness) that reconstructs depth and discharge at arbitrary query points. Pointwise decoding decouples memory from grid size and handles irregular watersheds natively, enabling metropolitan-scale training on a single compute node and direct queries at exact gauge coordinates without raster snapping. We evaluate CLDNet on a synthetic -cell Texas benchmark and on a new Des Plaines case study of real-rainfall Stage IV storms whose reference simulator we validate against United States Geological Survey (USGS) gauges at the April 2013 flood-of-record (Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency on mean-recentered water-surface elevation). CLDNet reduces the relative root-mean-squared error of an unconditional baseline by , outperforms regular-grid VAE–ConvLSTM and FNO baselines on the Texas benchmark (both presuppose a Cartesian grid and do not apply to the irregular Des Plaines watershed), reaches a critical success index of at the inundation threshold, and produces a full -hour basin-wide forecast in seconds—a speedup. Finally, we demonstrate that CLDNet’s compact latent state supports online observation coupling: using the Latent Dynamics Ensemble Score Filter (LD-EnSF), we assimilate water-depth observations at gauge locations into the surrogate’s latent dynamics and recover a mean Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of against USGS observations at six held-out gauges, from for the rainfall-perturbed open-loop forecast, realizing the observation-update step required of an AI-driven flood digital twin.

title: AnytimeHydroTwin: A deployment-valid inference-orchestration layer for AI-driven hydrological digital twins
abstract: When does a water-quality nowcast need a process-resolving model, and when is the previous observation enough? Across eleven regimes on three tidal-estuarine systems, the answer is set by the signal, not the model. Estuarine pH and dissolved oxygen are persistence-dominated everywhere (lag-1 autocorrelation – ): a high-fidelity (HF) neural nowcaster beats the previous observation in none of the nine such regimes. Only Sacramento Delta 15-min turbidity genuinely decorrelates ( ), reflecting episodic sediment resuspension, and it alone rewards HF ( ). Variability is not the discriminant—the two highest-variance regimes are persistence-dominated—giving an operational screen: above , an expensive nowcaster will not repay its compute. We exploit this with AnytimeHydroTwin , an inference-orchestration layer rather than a full digital twin, whose deployment-valid pre-HF causal gate reads only observations available before the HF forward pass, so a skipped HF call is a real compute saving, not a post-hoc blend ratio. The gate is itself paid every step: an HF-invocation rate is not a compute saving, and we account for it in full. Our headline is a leakage-clean nested-split evaluation on Sacramento turbidity—NSE parity with HF-only, at HF, an estimated to end-to-end wall-clock saving from measured component latencies—closed for the two LSTM headline regimes, open for the TCN stress case and ancillary CAMELS variant. On the nine persistence-dominated regimes it safely defers to lag-1 of the time. This regime classification is robust across the three backbone families we evaluate (TCN, LSTM and Transformer): the structure reflects the signal more than the learner.

title: Deep learning with upstream-aware terrain representations and rainfall adapter for generalizable pluvial flood prediction
abstract: Deep learning-based surrogate models can substantially accelerate pluvial flood simulations. However, most existing approaches struggle to generalize across heterogeneous terrains or modified topographies, limiting their applicability for real-world flood risk assessment unless retrained for each specific terrain.In this work, we investigate how deep learning flood surrogates can be designed to achieve robust spatial generalization across previously unseen terrain configurations without retraining. We train models on diverse terrain and introduce upstream-aware input maps that propagate terrain properties into downstream regions, allowing the model to capture long-range spatial dependencies and supporting the learning of more generalizable spatial features. In addition, we add architectural design choices to improve the model’s capacity to generalize beyond the training domain. We further propose a two-stage training strategy with an adapter-like rainfall encoder that enables efficient adaptation to previously unseen rainfall intensities while preserving spatial generalizability.The resulting model predicts maximum water depths and is evaluated on unseen catchments in Austria and Denmark, as well as on artificially modified terrains such as dikes. Our results demonstrate that combining a large training dataset with upstream-aware terrain representations and a generalization-oriented architectural design enables accurate flood predictions across unseen terrains and rainfall scenarios, reaching a RMSE below $0.05$ and CSI$_{0.3}$ of up to $0.91$ in test cases, outperforming previous models in both prediction accuracy and Critical Success Index.

title: Hydrologically constrained genetic programming for interpretable rainfall–runoff model discovery: A process–informed machine learning approach
abstract: Advances in machine learning have improved rainfall–runoff prediction, but integrating these capabilities with interpretable, process-based model structures remains an open challenge. This study seeks a middle ground between conceptual hydrological modelling and modern data-driven prediction by automating model structure discovery while retaining interpretability and hydrological consistency. We introduce HydroXGP (Hydrological Model eXplorer using Genetic Programming) to reduce reliance on legacy model choices and subjective a priori structural assumptions by learning model structure directly from data during optimization. The framework evolves models from a modular, process-based component library adapted from the open-source MARRMoT toolbox, making the search process-informed through reusable flux and routing components and hydrologically constrained by enforcing mass balance during simulation. GP jointly optimizes model structure and parameters, while each discovered model remains explicit and interpretable. Evaluation on the CAMELS-US dataset showed that a proof-of-concept test in a snow-dominated basin achieved strong performance over the out-of-sample test period (NSE=0.849), and, when transferred to a hydrologically similar basin, the learned structure retained useful predictive skill (NSE=0.724). Across 18 basins (one representative basin per U.S. hydrologic region), median NSE reached 0.702, generally outperforming the mean performance of an ensemble of conceptual benchmark models while remaining competitive with some regional LSTM baselines. The findings support a modelling perspective in which structural hypotheses can be revisited and adapted as new data, diagnostics, or environmental signals become available, enabling basin-specific configurations that evolve in response to changing information rather than relying on a single fixed template.

title: Hybrid physics–AI modeling in hydrogeology: a review of concepts, applications, and challenges
abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping hydrogeological modeling. The question is whether hybrid physics–AI approaches can reconcile the explanatory power of process-based models with the flexibility and speed of machine learning. We try to answer this question with a concept-driven review which traces the progression from purely data-driven approaches to emerging modeling paradigms incorporating physical knowledge. We show that hydrogeological modeling is moving beyond a simple opposition between mechanistic simulators and black-box algorithms toward a continuum of physics–AI integration, including theory-guided machine learning, physics-informed neural networks, physics-aware architectures, neural operators, generative models, and differentiable programming. Applications across key hydrogeological domains are reviewed, followed by a discussion of current limitations and barriers to operational deployment, including data requirements, transferability across hydrogeological settings, verification and validation, uncertainty quantification, and issues of trust. We conclude that hybrid physics–AI modeling should not be understood as a replacement for hydrogeological theory, but as an emerging methodological framework in which physical laws, numerical simulation, and machine learning are combined to produce models that are faster, more interpretable, more robust, and more useful for decision-making in groundwater science and management.

title: Deep learning meets spectral analysis: reproducing long-term persistence in synthetic streamflow
abstract: Synthetic streamflow generation requires simultaneous reproduction of flow distributions and temporal dependence across multiple scales, including long-term persistence (LTP). This study evaluates a three-stage framework that combines latent-space generation with a temporal convolutional network (TCN), low-frequency spectral adjustment, and quantile-based rank reordering. The framework was applied to daily discharge records from 24 UK river basins and benchmarked against autoregressive moving average (ARMA), k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN), and long short-term memory (LSTM) generators. Marginal distributions were reproduced closely (median Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic = 0.00069; 99th-percentile ratios = 0.986–0.999). The median absolute difference in the rescaled-range persistence estimate was 0.028, with 79% of basins within a tolerance of 0.05. Detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) produced a median scaling-exponent difference of 0.076; Monte Carlo tests showed that part of the R/S-DFA discrepancy reflects estimator-specific finite-sample behavior. The same experiments indicate that a 0.05 tolerance is approximately a two-standard-deviation band at the 7,300-day synthetic-series length, and that shorter records tend to inflate persistence estimates. ARMA produced a statistically indistinguishable median R/S error (0.024). For the nine records with no missing days, the proposed framework and k-NN showed very similar paired low-flow spell-duration errors. The proposed framework is therefore not uniformly superior to simpler alternatives; its main value is the combination of close marginal matching with an explicit spectral mechanism for controlling long-term persistence. Remaining limitations include weaker short-lag autocorrelation reproduction and incomplete recovery of threshold-conditioned spell clustering.

title: A large-scale molecular dynamics investigation of anisotropic hydraulic conductivity in compacted clay system
abstract: This study developed a large-scale molecular dynamics framework to investigate anisotropic hydraulic conductivity by linking directional water transport to compaction state, platelet fabric, and surface chemistry. A total of 150 multi-particle nanoflow models were constructed across dry densities ( ρ d ) of 1.2–1.8 g·cm −3 , orientational order parameters ( S ) of 0.60 to 0.92, and cation exchange capacities (CEC) of 0.11–97.44 cmol·kg −1 . Simulated hydraulic conductivities ranged from 0.77 × 10 -14 to 1.96 × 10 -12 m·s −1 , with 97.0% of available experimental measurements falling within this envelope. Mean horizontal hydraulic conductivity ( k h ) consistently exceeded mean vertical hydraulic conductivity ( k v ) by factors of approximately 2.4–5.6. Increasing dry density narrowed water-accessible pores, reduced independent spanning pathways and critical spanning diameters, and increased tortuosity, thereby decreasing both k h and k v . Platelet orientation differentiated the two flow directions by maintaining more direct horizontal pathways. Increasing CEC shifted pore water toward Na associated states and reduced the flux carried by interfacial only and free water, further lowering both k h and k v . Random Forest models achieved mean testing R 2 values of 0.92 for k h and 0.88 for k v and identified dry density as the dominant descriptor in both directions. Platelet orientation had a greater relative influence on vertical than horizontal conductivity, whereas CEC made a smaller but consistent contribution. Fixed-density sensitivity analysis showed that increasing dry density shifted the relative sensitivity weight from platelet orientation toward CEC, particularly for k v . These findings clarify the distinct structural and physicochemical controls on directional water transport and hydraulic anisotropy in compacted clay barriers.

title: A prototype multi-hazard early warning system integrating flood and landslide forecasting: application in the upper Garonne River Basin
abstract: Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS) are essential for disaster risk management, yet operational implementation remains limited by challenges in hazard integration, forecast uncertainty, and computational requirements. This study develops and evaluates a fast and lightweight prototype MHEWS integrating fluvial flooding and shallow landslide forecasting. The MHEWS couples snow-hydrological modeling (SNOW-17 and CREST) with a slope stability approach (infinite slope and Random Forest models) driven by bias-corrected Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS) meteorological forecasts. Quantile mapping bias correction substantially improves precipitation and temperature forecast performance, reducing variability errors and enhancing distributional agreement. Applied in the Upper Garonne River Basin (Spanish Pyrenees) using 24-hour lead time forecasts, multi-hazard analysis for 2010–2020 reveals asymmetric coupling between hazards: flood warnings respond rapidly to rainfall intensity, while landslide warnings depend on cumulative subsurface conditioning and antecedent soil moisture, with high-level warnings rarely coinciding. Evaluation of multiple forecast lead times (24, 48, 72 h) for June 2013 demonstrates systematic performance degradation with increasing lead time, reflecting amplified uncertainty propagation. This degradation is further compounded by the limitations of the quantile mapping approach; while it effectively aligns marginal statistics, it fails to preserve temporal autocorrelation or event persistence. This introduces residual biases in cumulative dynamics that disproportionately affect landslide prediction compared to flood estimation. The fully automated prototype, designed to be scalable and transferable, and built on open-source software and cloud infrastructure, demonstrates operational feasibility for real-time early warning applications across hydro-meteorologically complex environments.

title: Streamflow prediction in natural ungauged catchments using Temporal Fusion Transformers
abstract: Streamflow prediction is essential for water resources management. Classical hydrological models struggle with predictive accuracy and probabilistic representation in ungauged catchments. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated notable improvements in reproducing complex time series, such as streamflow, with the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) emerging as a promising model. This study explores the potential of TFTs to predict daily streamflow in natural ungauged catchments in Portugal. Streamflow data from 53 catchments were collected from the national database, while meteorological inputs (precipitation and temperature) were derived from the ERA5-Land reanalysis dataset. Geomorphological descriptors for each catchment were also included. Results are reported on 46 catchments after screening from the initial set based on objective hydrometric and natural-flow criteria and show strong predictive performance and spatial generalization under ungauged conditions. In the test subsets, TFT models in ungauged conditions outperformed individually calibrated hydrological models Hydrologiska Byråns Vattenbalansavdelning (HBV), securing advantage in terms of median NSE (increased from 0.46 to 0.50), median KGE (increased from 0.44 to 0.48) and median CRPS (decreased, which is desired, from 5.51 to 3.75 ). Model specialization significantly improved performance, reaching a median NSE = 0.62, a median KGE = 0.65, and the median CRPS decreases to 3.20 , in selected test portions for this second task. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models were also evaluated as a data-driven benchmark, with TFTs achieving competitive performance under ungauged conditions. Additionally, retraining experiments highlight the model’s adaptability, showing that local data, even if limited in number, can be instrumental in further improving predictions. These findings support the application of deep learning in operational settings, such as flood and drought risk management, and water allocation strategies in catchments without comprehensive measurements.

title: Global patterns of reservoir normal water storage capacities estimated by statistical and machine learning models
abstract: Reservoir water storages are increasingly recognized as important tools for adapting to water-related hazards under climate change, particularly through their normal water storage (NWS). However, a critical data gap on regarding global reservoir NWS hinders our understanding of their spatial patterns and impacts on water management. This study aims to bridge this data gap by estimating the NWS for 7,250 global reservoirs using an ensemble approach that includes linear regression, machine learning, and satellite-based methods. We train and evaluate these models based on a representative sample of 801 reservoirs with reported NWS data and multiple static attributes. Among the evaluated methods, the Gradient Boosted Decision Trees model utilizing various reservoir features performed best (achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.95 and a mean absolute percentage error of 12%), and was subsequently selected to estimate the NWS for unrecorded reservoirs. Our analysis of the global reservoir NWS ratio (NWSR) at individual, basin, and national scales reveals significant spatial variations, with a global mean NWSR of 72%. The distribution of NWSRs varies considerably across different reservoir groups categorized by physical size, primary purpose, and climatic region. At the national and basin scales, the USA, Canada, China, Russia, and Brazil, along with the Yenisey, Nile, Mississippi, Parana, and Yangtze basins, account for substantial portions of the global NWS capacity. The developed dataset and the analyzed spatial patterns provide vital empirical inputs for water resource management, large-scale hydrological modeling, and climate change adaptation, ultimately supporting effective planning for sustainable freshwater supplies.

title: Effects of droughts and warm months on phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations in surface waters globally
abstract: Phosphorus (P) and nitrogen (N) concentrations in surface waters are substantially affected by droughts and warm months. However, previous studies of phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations under these hydro-climatic extremes are limited to a small number of regions, mainly in parts of North America, Europe and Australia. Here we perform the first global-scale analysis of phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations in surface waters under droughts, warm months and compound drought-warm months for the period 1980–2010. To achieve this, we developed an approach to downscale existing simulation data of total phosphorus (TP) and total nitrogen (TN) concentrations from annual to monthly level with machine learning at 0.5 × 0.5 degree resolution. The results indicate generally mixed responses in phosphorus and nitrogen concentrations under drought, with some regions showing increases in the concentrations of phosphorus and nitrogen due to drought and others showing decreases. Additionally, the results show more consistent increases in phosphorus (P) concentrations during warm months (average change: +21%) and compound drought-warm months (average change: +10%), which was mainly attributed to less dilution during periods of low flow and high temperature. Furthermore, there is a general decrease in the N:P ratio observed globally during warm months (average change: −11%). The results from this study provide a broader understanding of the effects of droughts and warm months on phosphorus and nitrogen in surface waters compared to previous local-scale studies. Furthermore, the results highlight the significant changes in phosphorus and nitrogen ratios during droughts and warm months, which may significantly influence freshwater ecosystem health worldwide.

title: High-frequency monitoring and reconstruction of lake water temperature with meteorological observations
abstract: Lakes, as vital components of land water systems, play crucial roles in local climate regulation and ecological functions. Water temperature is a key indicator of lake thermal dynamics and climate sensitivity, while its high-frequency variations and coupling mechanisms with meteorological drivers remain insufficiently understood, especially under extreme weather conditions. To bridge this gap, we conducted a detailed investigation of Qinghai Lake using high-resolution (1 h interval) observations of water temperature and meteorological variables from October 2023 to October 2024. We developed a comprehensive analytical framework incorporating statistical analysis, wavelet time–frequency decomposition, anomaly detection, and deep learning-based reconstruction. The results reveal a strong nonlinear relationship between water and air temperature, as demonstrated by RAPS trend analysis and S-curve regression (R2 = 0.82). Wavelet coherence analysis indicates robust coupling at diurnal and synoptic timescales, with a distinct temporal lag in the lake’s thermal response to atmospheric forcing. Anomaly detection further highlights the critical role of strong wind and precipitation in driving abrupt water temperature shifts. To improve reconstruction performance, we propose a novel PCA-GRU-MA model, which integrates Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Multi-Head Attention mechanisms (MA). Model validation demonstrates superior accuracy compared to seven benchmark models (RMSE = 1.55 °C, MAE = 1.15 °C, NSE = 0.94), underscoring its capacity to capture thermal anomalies and effectiveness in reconstructing hourly water temperature. This study advances the understanding of high-resolution lake thermal dynamics and offers a methodological foundation for lake ecosystem management, climate change adaptation, and early-warning systems.

title: Hydrogeological controls on seasonal groundwater level dynamics across Greece: A national-scale assessment integrating monitoring data, earth observation, and interpretable machine learning (2013–2022)
abstract: Groundwater monitoring networks typically provide broad spatial coverage but sparse and irregular temporal observations, which limit their direct use for operational groundwater status assessment. Mediterranean groundwater systems are subject to strong seasonal contrasts between winter recharge and summer abstraction, yet national-scale assessments resolving how aquifer type modulates this signal remain scarce. We analyzed 22,281 quality-controlled groundwater level records from 2,477 monitoring wells across the 14 River Basin Districts of Greece (2013 to 2022), drawn from the WISE database of the European Environment Agency, combining stratified non-parametric statistics with an interpretable XGBoost classification framework for screening of deeper-than-normal groundwater conditions. Seasonal dynamics differed systematically by aquifer type (Kruskal-Wallis H = 32.37, p = 9.34 × 10 −8 ). Porous aquifers showed the smallest seasonal amplitude (σ = 5.36 m) and the strongest coupling with root-zone soil moisture (Spearman ρ = +0.228), consistent with diffuse vertical Darcian recharge. Karstic aquifers exhibited intermediate amplitude (σ = 6.42 m) with a marked elevation gradient in dry-season drawdown, from + 0.79 m at low elevation to + 2.83 m above 300 m, reflecting dual-porosity behaviour in upland carbonate massifs. Fractured-rock aquifers displayed the largest amplitude (σ = 6.83 m) and effectively no soil-moisture coupling (ρ = +0.020), consistent with preferential recharge bypassing the soil column. The divergence in soil-moisture sensitivity between porous and fractured systems is the clearest statistical contrast in the dataset and is consistent with a difference in dominant recharge pathway, although the observational design does not allow that mechanism to be established directly. Within porous aquifers, sites combining high cropland cover and high vegetation vigour showed net summer recovery (Δh = − 0.42 m, Mann-Whitney p = 2.79 × 10 −3 ), a signal consistent with irrigation return flow that was statistically absent in karstic and fractured systems (p > 0.3). Among wells with continuous records over 2018 to 2022, 61.7% showed net decline and 100 wells (6.8%) showed persistent drawdown above 2 m per measurement interval, concentrated in Thessaly and the Messara plain; with only five annual values and irregular observation intervals, these are reported as short-period changes among repeatedly monitored wells rather than as national depletion trends. A station-standardized XGBoost classifier achieved ROC AUC = 0.695 on an independent 2021 to 2022 test set, with SHAP attribution identifying seasonal phase, antecedent soil moisture, annual precipitation, and potential evapotranspiration as the leading physically coherent predictors. The findings support consideration of aquifer-type-stratified reference conditions within the Water Framework Directive and provide a quantitative basis for prioritising monitoring investments in karstic and fractured-rock systems.

title: Human proximity to rivers in China
abstract: River proximity shapes human settlement patterns and water resource dependence, yet the long-term changes of human–river proximity and their drivers remain poorly understood. Using high-resolution population data for ten reference years, we developed a Proximity to Rivers Index (PRI) to quantify changes in population-density gradients relative to major rivers across China from 1953 to 2020. Random Forest models and counterfactual scenarios were used to examine socio-economic and natural associations with PRI. Despite a doubling of the population, the median population–river distance remained close to 10 km. However, PRI became progressively more negative from 1953 to 2020, indicating strengthening population concentration near rivers without a substantial shift in the median population location. Basin-scale trajectories were heterogeneous: human–river proximity generally strengthened in northern basins, whereas several southern basins exhibited weakening or more complex trends. Socio-economic variables were more strongly associated with the long-term PRI change, particularly in northern basins, while natural variability was more closely related to fluctuations among reference years in several southern basins. Urbanization rate and GDP had the highest relative importance nationally. Urban settlements were consistently closer to rivers than rural settlements, whereas the relationship between per-capita GDP and river proximity varied among Eastern, Central, and Western China. These findings highlight the need for basin-specific management that coordinates urban development, river-corridor protection, water-resource allocation, and climate adaptation.

title: SPECTRA-based detection of drug-induced hepatotoxicity through extracellular vesicle analysis
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EV) are becoming crucial targets in liquid biopsy, diagnostics, and therapeutic applications, yet their nanoscale characterization remains challenging. In this context, the detection of drug-induced liver injury, i.e., hepatotoxicity, through EV molecular content remains unexplored. To this end, we present the SPECTRA - S urface P lasmonic E nhancement with C ombined T ransformative RA man and Interferometric Microscopy approach, which provides rapid, label-free EV content analysis under 30 minutes and requires only 1.3 microliters of sample. Using hepatic cultures as a model, our platform captures distinct and reproducible EV molecular changes in response to acetaminophen-induced hepatotoxicity. Across independent culture sets, a Gaussian Process Regression model predicted Acetaminophen (APAP) dose with median absolute error of 1.50 mM and minimal bias (Bland-Altman bias ~0.03 mM); cross-validated RMSE was 3.145 mM. These findings establish EVs as dynamic reporters of cellular drug responses and demonstrate use of SPECTRA for EV detection of hepatotoxicity.

title: Machine learning-assisted electrochemical SERS for sensitive detection of multiple urinary proteins
abstract: In this study, we report the development and application of a plasmonic nanostructure-based surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) platform, integrated with electrochemical deposition and a convolutional neural network (CNN), for the sensitive and precise detection and quantification of kidney disease biomarkers in urine. A gold nanodimple (AuND) substrate was subjected to electrochemical deposition to produce a highly reproducible and sensitive SERS substrate for protein analysis. Evaluation of the performance of the platform through reproducibility tests and quantitative analysis of Cytochrome C protein demonstrated that it has a high sensitivity and a low detection limit of 8.2 pg/mL. The system was then applied to multiplexed analysis of three kidney disease-related proteins: albumin, transferrin (TrF), and immunoglobulin G (IgG). A combination of ANOVA-based feature selection and CNN classification models achieved high accuracy, with classification accuracies of 93.8% for albumin, 96.8% for TrF, and 96.8% for IgG. Subsequently, CNN-based regression models were utilized to quantify protein concentrations in urine samples, demonstrating robust performance with R 2 values of 0.9321 for albumin, 0.9848 for TrF, and 0.9957 for IgG. The method also exhibited excellent diagnostic feasibility, successfully detecting and quantifying target proteins in a urine matrix. The proposed platform thus offers a highly sensitive, reliable and non-invasive approach for early diagnosis of kidney diseases.

title: Machine learning-assisted colorimetric and photothermal detection of α-defensin using a competitive aptamer-based lateral flow biosensor with carbon nanotube tags
abstract: α-Defensin is a critical biomarker for joint infections such as periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), yet its rapid and sensitive detection remains challenging with conventional methods like ELISA and HPLC. Herein, we present a machine learning-assisted colorimetric and photothermal lateral flow biosensor for the sensitive and specific α-defensin detection in human samples. The biosensor adopts a competitive aptamer-based recognition mechanism, utilizes carbon nanotubes as dual-functional labels for visual and photothermal readouts, and integrates a machine learning algorithm to enhance detection accuracy. Molecular docking simulations were performed to clarify the binding mechanism between aptamer and α-defensin, thereby guiding the rational design of complementary DNA sequences and optimizing the competitive recognition strategy. The optimized biosensor demonstrated a wide detection range (5–5000 ng mL-1), a low limit of detection (4.01 ng mL-1), and high specificity against common interferents in synovial fluid. It also exhibited good repeatability and stability, and successfully discriminated infected from non-infected clinical synovial fluid samples. This integrated platform offers a portable, reliable, and user-friendly tool for point-of-care testing of α-defensin, and holds significant potential for clinical diagnostic applications.

title: TDM-OA-ICOS optical sensor for ppb-level C2H4 and CH4 simultaneous detection in postharvest fruit
abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of volatile gases is important for understanding fruit ripening processes, optimizing storage conditions, and ensuring food quality during postharvest storage. Ethylene (C2H4) acts as a key phytohormone regulating fruit ripening, while Methane (CH4) can serve as an indicator of microbial activity and spoilage-related biochemical processes. In this work, a high-sensitivity gas sensor based on Time-Division Multiplexed Off-Axis Integrated Cavity Output Spectroscopy (TDM-OA-ICOS) was developed for the simultaneous detection of C2H4 and CH4. To improve signal quality under complex storage environments, the demodulated 2f signals were processed using the Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (ICEEMDAN) algorithm to effectively suppress noise and reduce mode mixing. Furthermore, an optimized concentration inversion model combining the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (SBOA) with the Least Squares Support Vector Machine (LSSVM) was established to enhance the accuracy of gas concentration retrieval. The sensor exhibited excellent linear responses for both gases, with limits of detection of 4.43 ppb for C2H4 and 1.19 ppb for CH4, as determined by Allan variance analysis. These results indicate that the proposed TDM-OA-ICOS sensor provides strong potential for applications in postharvest quality assessment, controlled-atmosphere storage, fermentation process monitoring, and food spoilage diagnostics.

title: Unlocking practical calibration of sensor arrays for environmental applications through a hybrid physical and machine learning model approach
abstract: Ion-selective electrode (ISE) arrays have proven useful in medical and other applications, but their use for measurement of environmental waters has lagged. Data-driven (machine learning) models are necessary to recover usable information from ISE arrays as physical models are not generally invertible, however curating training datasets can be prohibitively expensive. This work poses the question: to what extent might well-vetted physical models of the sensors be leveraged to augment training of data-driven models, therein unlocking broader application of ISE-based sensor arrays? Using a 10-element ISE array responsive to the majority of surface water charge balance and N-nutrient ions, environmentally-representative training samples (n=273) were measured. An extended Nikolsky-Eisenman model was created (residual RMSE 1–20 mV per sensor/target ion) and used to generate significantly more synthetic data (n > 10,000) than collected experimentally. Non-linear machine learning (ML) models (random forests, support vector regression, artificial neural networks, symbolic regression, deep neural networks) were trained to estimate target ion concentration (potassium, ammonium, and nitrate) as a function of varying proportions of experimental and synthetic data and increasing dataset size. The value-add of the sensor array approach increased as target ISE membrane selectivity worsened while augmenting experimental data with physically simulated synthetic data (up to 50% of total training dataset) improved quality of machine learning models for ion targets lacking highly selective membranes. This suggests that for challenging ion targets in complex mixed samples embedding physical laws into the ML training has the potential to support accelerated ISE array development with less overall experimental lab work required.

title: Label-free SERS fingerprint recognition of salivary biomarkers for Parkinson’s disease using hierarchical silver nanogrooves and transfer learning
abstract: Non-invasive identification of neuroprotein biomarkers in complex biofluids using surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) remains challenging. To address this, we developed a hierarchical silver nanogroove SERS substrate combined with a transfer learning strategy for salivary neuroprotein analysis. The hierarchical nanosurface features nanogrooves decorated with nanosynapses, which multilevel architecture enables the confinement of neuroprotein biomarkers within the multidimensional ”hotspots” regions of its nanoscale cavities. Hierarchical silver nanogrooves enabled label-free SERS fingerprint recognition of key neuroprotein biomarkers, such as Aβ, Tau, α-Synuclein and their mixtures. Then, a transfer learning model, trained solely on pure SERS spectra of these three proteins, extracts molecular fingerprints without requiring large mixed-analyte datasets. And the pretrained model was applied to identify α-Synuclein signals in saliva samples from 40 Parkinson’s disease (PD) patients, enabling non-invasive detection without retraining, achieving a high detection probability of 0.9678. In binary and ternary mixtures of α-Synuclein, Aβ, and Tau, the transfer learning program specifically identified the target protein. All probabilities exceeded the classification threshold, demonstrating consistent recognition of α-Synuclein-specific signatures despite complex protein backgrounds and saliva matrices. In sum, a non-invasive, label-free SERS detection of neuroproteins for neurodegenerative diseases using a transfer learning-enhanced hierarchical silver nanogroove platform is presented, this approach offers a promising pathway to facilitate clinical translation of SERS technology and support the diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases, such as PD.

title: Strain-engineered active site migration and machine learning-assisted NO2 recognition in UV-activated Cs-doped WO3-x nanosheets with operando mechanistic insights
abstract: Pristine metal oxide gas sensors often suffer from poor selectivity and limited polarizability. To overcome these bottlenecks, oxygen vacancy-rich 2D ultrathin Cs-doped WO3-x nanosheets were synthesized via a solvothermal method. Advanced characterizations (KPFM, UPS, and TAS) confirmed that optimal Cs doping (0.08 mol%) optimizes the surface work function and drastically prolongs the photo-generated carrier lifetime (τ_3 = 40.45 ns), maximizing UV-excited charge separation. Consequently, under 365 nm UV illumination at 175℃, the sensor exhibited an ultra-high response of 118.4 to 10 ppm NO2, a 2.41 ppb limit of detection, ultra-fast kinetics (10 s/7 s response/recovery), superior immunity to moisture interference (stable across a 30% to 90% RH gradient), and robust 30-day long-term stability. To resolve cross-selectivity limitations, a machine learning model integrating Random Forest (RF) feature extraction and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) was deployed, achieving 98.8% recognition accuracy in multi-component gas mixtures. Mechanistically, in-situ/operando Raman Two-Dimensional Correlation Spectroscopy (2D-COS) and Density Functional Theory (DFT) revealed that steric hindrance from large Cs+ ions induces localized W-O lattice strain while effectively eliminating surface moisture side reactions. This strain creates distorted sites with ultra-high adsorption energy (-1.3538 eV), driving a ”complete migration” of NO2 active adsorption sites away from the intrinsic lattice. By coupling strain-engineered active site migration with artificial intelligence, this work provides a powerful blueprint for the next generation of highly selective, intelligent gas sensors.

title: Differential competitive mechanism-driven three-channel sensor array for machine learning-enabled organophosphorus pesticides identification
abstract: The rapid and accurate identification of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) is crucial for ensuring food safety. However, the discrimination of structurally similar pesticide analogues across varying concentrations remains a formidable challenge. In this work, a three-channel sensor array integrating dual-colorimetric and photothermal responses was developed using performance-optimized Au/MIL-100(Fe) nanozyme as recognition unit for the precise detection and intelligent discrimination of OPs. Mechanistic studies revealed that OPs inhibit catalytic activity by binding to the active centers of the nanozymes through coordination, thereby generating distinct signal patterns. Based on this response feature, a concentration-independent recognition model was established using artificial neural networks (ANN), achieving nearly 100% accurate identification of five types of OPs. The sensor array reached a picomolar (pM) limit of detection, and maintained excellent anti-interference capability and stability in complex matrices (tap water, cabbage, and peaches), offering a versatile tool for high-throughput, intelligent pesticide residue screening.

title: Prognostic model for pancreatic cancer based on machine learning of routine slides and transcriptomic tumor analysis
authors: on behalf of the GTK Pancreatic Cancer Study Group in Japan
abstract: Background Prognostication for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) using histologic images is difficult due to tumor heterogeneity. Image patches from hematoxylin and eosin-stained slides were clustered via uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) and used to train a random forest model. Predictive performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Gene expression analysis was conducted to characterise survival-related clusters. Results Seventeen patch clusters were identified. Two were linked to high recurrence risk, and one to low risk. In external validation, the model achieved an AUC of up to 0.792. The random forest score independently predicted recurrence. verified_metadata.title: Prognostic model for pancreatic cancer based on machine learning of routine slides and transcriptomic tumor analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Background Prognostication for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) using histologic images is difficult due to tumor heterogeneity. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI) model to predict postoperative recurrence using histologic image patches. Methods We included 591 patients with resected PDAC to train an AI model for recurrence prediction at 12 or 24 months and validated it using external cohorts (n = 302 in total). Image patches from hematoxylin and eosin-stained slides were clustered via uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) and used to train a random forest model. Predictive performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Gene expression analysis was conducted to characterise survival-related clusters. Results Seventeen patch clusters were identified. Two were linked to high recurrence risk, and one to low risk. In external validation, the model achieved an AUC of up to 0.792. The random forest score independently predicted recurrence. Greater heterogeneity in patch composition correlated with shorter time to recurrence (P < 0.01). High-risk clusters showed elevated CSF3R expression; the low-risk cluster showed increased IGFBP3 expression. Conclusions Our AI model, using only archival histologic slides, accurately predicted postoperative recurrence in PDAC and revealed image features linked to outcomes and gene expression.

title: Economic evaluation of artificial intelligence for cancer detection in the UK breast screening programme
abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a potential solution to radiologist shortages in breast cancer screening while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. Retrospective studies suggest AI performs comparably to human readers in detecting cancers, but no economic evaluations have yet used prospective trial data. Methods We developed a de novo discrete-event simulation model to estimate the cost-effectiveness of integrating AI into the NHS screening pathway using evidence from a large prospective trial. Results The AI-only strategy generated a small incremental QALY gain of 0.00009 and reduced lifetime costs by £159.55 per woman invited, and had a 100% probability of being most cost-effective at the £20,000/QALY threshold. Replacing one human reader with AI also increased QALYs, by 0.00019, and reduced costs by £31.07. Triple reading (two humans plus AI) produced the largest QALY gain (0.00023) but increased costs by £72.79. All AI-based pathways reduced cancer deaths, shifted cancers from advanced (TNM stage 4) to earlier stages at detection, and increased the proportion of cancers detected by screening. Conclusion Using AI in place of human readers is likely to be cost-effective, marginally improving health outcomes while reducing overall costs, with full replacement of both human readers being the most cost-effective screening strategy.

title: Integrated multi-omics and single-cell analyses identify metabolic heterogeneity and therapeutic vulnerabilities in medullary thyroid cancer
abstract: Background Medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) is a heterogeneous and aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options. Metabolic reprogramming, a hallmark of cancer, may offer a promising avenue for understanding and managing MTC. Methods RNA sequencing data of 101 MTC samples were obtained from a published dataset PRJCA008783, and untargeted metabolomic profiling was performed on 51 paired samples. Metabolic subtypes were identified using clustering analyses and validated using immunohistochemistry (47 cases), multiplex immunofluorescence (12 cases), and a previously published single-cell RNA sequencing dataset (7 cases derived from PRJCA021386). Deep learning-based approaches were applied to develop prognostic models. Results Three metabolic subtypes were identified. The M3 subtype, associated with poor prognosis, was characterised by upregulated glycosaminoglycan (GAGs) biosynthesis, particularly chondroitin sulfate, and elevated expression of CHSY1, a key GAGs biosynthetic enzyme. M3 tumours displayed enhanced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) signatures. Multi-omic analyses implicated CHSY1 may promote EMT through interactions with myofibroblasts, which was supported by immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence. Two prognostic classifiers, the 8 Metabolites Model and the 28 Metabolic Genes Model, effectively stratified patients by recurrence risk, with predictive power largely driven by GAGs-associated metabolism. Conclusions Our study reveals substantial metabolic heterogeneity in MTC and proposes a novel metabolic classification system, offering mechanistic insights and supporting metabolite-driven prognostication for precision management of MTC.

title: Lactylation-related prognostic signature characterized in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma through public scRNA-seq dataset and machine learning algorithms: the TOP2A-H3K18la-NQO1 axis orchestrates malignant progression
abstract: Background Lactate promotes histone lactylation, which affects protein transcription and translation, thereby influencing tumour cell progression. However, the role of lactylation in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains underexplored and warrants further investigation. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data (GSE154778) underwent quality control, dimensionality reduction, and clustering. Lactylation scores were computed using the "AUCell" R package, and differential expression between high and low lactylation groups was analysed. A risk score model based on lactylation was developed using TCGA-PAAD, GSE57495, and GSE79668 datasets. The relationships between risk scores, clinical features, immune profiles, mutation burden, and biological functions were assessed. CUT&Tag analysis was employed to identify the target of TOP2A mediated by H3K18la. In vitro experiments, including CCK-8 assay, colony formation assay, wound healing assay, transwell migration assay, lactate quantification, Western blotting, and qRT‒PCR, in combination with subcutaneous xenograft models, were conducted to further validate the findings. Results We successfully established a lactylation-based prognostic risk score model for PDAC, which effectively distinguishes patient survival and biological characteristics. Additionally, we demonstrated that the lactate-TOP2A-H3K18la-NQO1 signalling axis forms a positive feedback loop that accelerates the malignant progression of PDAC. Conclusions This study presents a lactylation-related risk score model with significant potential for improving the management of PDAC patients. The identification of the lactate-TOP2A-H3K18la-NQO1 axis enhances the understanding of lactylation mechanisms in PDAC, thereby providing a foundation for targeted therapeutic approaches.

title: Signatures of micropeptides encoded by lncRNAs in cancer progression and metastasis
abstract: Abstract Background Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate gene expression, chromatin organization, and cellular signaling. Although traditionally considered non-coding, 21% of the ~190,000 annotated lncRNA transcripts contain poorly characterized open reading frames with unknown function. Methods We systematically identified lncRNAs encoding micropeptides (MPs) using integrated computational and experimental evidence. Expression profiles across 17 cancer types from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed to identify cancer-associated and transitional lncRNAs (Tr-lncRNAs). Structural modeling using AlphaFold was further applied to predict folding. Results We identified 478 lncRNA genes encoding 1782 MPs (10–100 amino acids). These MPs exhibit distinct amino acid and dipeptide compositions and are enriched for specific 4-mer motifs compared with canonical proteins. A subset of lncRNAs, including TNN-AS1, PVT1, XIST, and SNHG family members, encode multiple MPs. Analysis across cancer stages identified 2399 Tr-lncRNAs, most of them were cancer type and stage specific. Among these, 314 highly confident MPs from 72 Tr-lncRNAs were further analyzed. Pan-cancer analysis suggested MP-like functions for Tr-lncRNAs such as LINC01234, HAND2-AS1, XIST, UCA1, and HOXA11-AS. While most MPs are predicted to be intrinsically disordered, 3D structural modeling revealed several MPs with stable folds, including ubiquitin-like and RNase H-like structures. Conclusions Tr-lncRNA–derived MPs represent a previously underexplored class of potentially functional molecules associated with cancer clinical annotation and may serve as biomarkers for disease progression.

ORR was 56.12% in patients with PD-L1 CPS ≥ 5 and 36.73% in those with CPS Conclusions In conclusion, we developed a cPCR-based model and risk-score system that more accurately forecasts nivolumab response in GC, offering a promising tool for optimising immunotherapy selection.

title: Abundant CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in glioblastoma harbor distinct exhaustion signatures in potentially reactive subsets
abstract: Background The effectiveness of immunotherapy against glioblastoma (GBM) remains limited, suggesting that antigen-specific tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are rare. This study aimed to identify tumor-specific T cells in GBM as the basis for antigen-specific immunotherapy. Methods Tumor specimens were collected from 56 patients newly diagnosed with IDH-wildtype GBM. In cases showing prominent intratumoral T-cell infiltration, CD3⁺CD8⁺CD4⁻ T cells were sorted for single-cell RNA and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing. Integrated analyses were performed using our single-cell dataset from the Aichi Cancer Center (ACC), publicly available GBM TILs datasets (PA), and lung cancer TILs and malignant pleural effusions datasets (LC). Candidate reactive TCRs were identified using an AI-based algorithm. Results Unsupervised analysis identified a dominant cluster characterized by the strong expression of exhaustion markers, most prominently LAG3, with high TCR clonality. Moreover, LAG3 and CXCL13 expression levels were significantly higher in the ACC TIL-rich subset than the PA dataset. Finally, a prediction algorithm suggested that our TIL-rich subset harbored a markedly higher proportion of potentially reactive T cells than the PA and LC datasets. Conclusions TILs with marked clonal expansion in certain GBM cases may include potentially reactive T cells with distinct exhaustion features, providing a foundation for the development of antigen-specific and LAG-3-targeted immunotherapies.

title: Vascular cognitive impairment and dementia: Prevention, treatments, mechanisms and management options for the future
abstract: Abstract Vascular Cognitive Impairment and Dementia (VCID), the second most common form of dementia, is becoming increasingly prevalent worldwide. However, currently there are no FDA-approved therapies for VCID. In this review, we explore treatments with extant supporting evidence as well as treatments in development and outline the path forward for future research. Donepezil, rivastigmine, and memantine all have some evidence as cognitive enhancers in patients with Vascular Dementia (VaD) and are approved in several non-US jurisdictions. Nutraceuticals, such as Ginkgo biloba and butylphthalide, have some supportive data and may be similarly helpful. Prevention of VCID is an important objective, and there is support for the intensive control of hypertension and treatment of hyperglycemia to prevent cognitive decline. Asymptomatic cerebral small vessel disease is commonly detected in neuropsychiatric cohorts and healthy individuals, and protocols and trials are being developed to help guide management to minimize the risk of cognitive impairment. A range of novel treatment strategies, including noninvasive neurostimulation, stimulant treatment, and neurotrophic factors, are being explored. Future research into VCID treatment needs to incorporate a range of novel technologies, including blood-based biomarkers, automation of brain image segmentation and quantification using artificial intelligence, automated remotely administered neuropsychological testing, and rational drug discovery.

title: The role of brain health and resilience in reshaping trajectories of late-life neuropsychiatric disorders
abstract: Abstract Global population aging and increased chronic stress due to numerous mass disasters including those related to pandemics, climate change, war, displacement, and political unrest all challenge our collective resilience, with a growing burden of late-life neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders placing unprecedented demands on health and social systems worldwide. With these considerations in mind, understanding and promoting brain health is becoming a priority for the prevention of neuropsychiatric disorders across the lifespan. Brain health represents a dynamic balance of neural, cognitive, and emotional processes that determine resilience to neuropsychiatric illness. In later life, this balance becomes particularly critical as neurobiological and psychosocial stressors converge to shape trajectories of neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. This review synthesizes current evidence on the determinants of brain health in aging, emphasizing resilience as a modifiable pathway linking neuropsychiatric illness risk and prevention. We integrate insights from neuroscience, lifestyle medicine, geroscience, and social determinants of health to emphasize the value of a whole-person, life-course approach. Particular attention is given to the interplay between stress physiology, interoceptive regulation, emotional resilience, and cognitive and brain reserve across the aging continuum. Emerging frameworks including brain clocks, precision biomarkers, digital phenotyping, and artificial intelligence, are considered as tools for risk stratification, early detection, and personalized intervention. By linking resilience mechanisms to measurable biological indices, we argue for the integration of neurobiological, psychological, behavioral, and sociocultural domains to inform next-generation strategies in neuropsychopharmacology, prevention science, and the promotion of healthy brain aging.

title: Mechanistic signatures of comorbid PTSD with cognitive impairment implicate cortisol-induced neural toxicity
abstract: Abstract The men and women who worked in rescue and recovery operations at the 9/11 World Trade Center site are developing cognitive impairment (CI) at mid-life, decades before CI is usually detected. To date, one of the most consistent risk factors for CI in this population is symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). However, little is known about the mechanistic cascade that drives stress-related neurological changes to accelerate cognitive decline in the human brain. We used machine learning to identify distinct brain signatures from functional magnetic resonance imaging between trauma-exposed healthy controls (TEHC; N = 30; 21 men), PTSD without CI (PTSD-CI; N = 19; 16 men), and PTSD with CI (PTSD + CI; N = 22; 18 men). We compared the spatial gradient of each functional signature to the distribution of mRNA expression in the brain. We applied structural equation modeling (SEM) to infer mechanistic cascades specific to each group. While modest accuracy was achieved for the PTSD–CI versus TEHC signature (0.67), clear differentiation was observed for PTSD + CI versus TEHC (0.73) and PTSD + CI versus PTSD–CI (0.85). Consistent significant correlations were found between PTSD + CI signatures and ZNF48 , TOMM40 , and GRIN1 expression distributions. The cortisol-induced neurotoxicity pathway was consistently found with the PTSD + CI signature, while the p53 signaling pathway was observed across all PTSD signatures. Our results reinforce peripheral biomarkers from a previous transcriptomic study and suggest functional biomarkers in PTSD and PTSD-related CI. Furthermore, our SEM results suggest that PTSD and PTSD-related CI may diverge at the mechanistic level, with neurotoxicity being specific to CI.

title: Semantic encoding of trauma memories in the hippocampus among individuals with PTSD
abstract: Abstract The recall of traumatic memories is central to clinical and neurobiological models of PTSD, yet neurocircuitry mechanisms underlying traumatic memory recall remain elusive. Recent advances in natural language processing and large language models enable complex semantic quantification of autobiographical memories. Here, we leveraged these analytic approaches to define the neurocircuitry encoding the semantic content of traumatic autobiographical narratives among individuals with PTSD. 79 women with PTSD related to interpersonal violence listened to traumatic and neutral autobiographical narratives during fMRI. Sentence-level brain activity and semantic embeddings were quantified for each script and participant. Neurocircuitry encoding semantic content of the narratives was defined through cross-validation across participants. A priori regions of interest included the hippocampus, superior temporal gyrus (STG), and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC). Our approach detected significant hippocampal sensitivity for semantic content of both trauma and neutral narratives; however, spatial encoding patterns of semantic content within the hippocampus differed between trauma and neutral narratives. Specifically, spatial encoding patterns in CA1 and dentate gyrus differentiated narrative type. Regardless of narrative type, PTSD symptom severity was positively associated with semantic encoding across the hippocampus and its subfields, except for the subiculum. For trauma narratives, semantic sensitivity was greater within the left STG and decreased in the PCC and broader default mode network. Encoding in neither region tracked with PTSD symptom severity. These results reveal a hippocampal role in mediating recall of specific semantic content for traumatic and neutral autobiographical narratives and suggest hippocampal sensitivity to autobiographical semantic content underlies greater PTSD symptom severity. title: Prenatal serotonin reuptake inhibitor exposure and maternal depression symptoms are associated with altered fetal brain and placental development
abstract: Abstract Maternal mental health is associated with fetal neurodevelopment. Identifying effective treatments for maternal psychiatric conditions is a public health priority. SRIs (SSRIs and SNRIs) are commonly prescribed for prenatal mental health conditions; however, their impact on fetal brain development remains understudied. In this observational cohort study, we compared fetal brain and placental structures between SRI-exposed and unexposed pregnancies divided by categories of maternal depressive symptom severity from the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Pregnant women treated with SRIs and controls without mental illness or antidepressant exposure underwent fetal MRI studies between 20-40 weeks’ gestation. Fetal brain motion correction and 3D reconstructions were performed using slice-to-volume registration. Fetal brain volumes (cortical gray matter, white matter, deep gray matter, cerebellum, brainstem, and hippocampi) were quantified using deep learning-based segmentation with manual correction. Cerebral cortical folding measures included local gyrification index, sulcal depth, curvedness, and surface area. Placental volume and microstructure were assessed with T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted MRI, respectively. EPDS scores were categorized as low ( ≤ 4), moderate (5–9), and high ( ≥ 10). A total of 182 pregnant women were included [62 SRI-exposed (59 SSRIs, 3 SNRIs); 120 controls]. Notably, 29% of SRI-exposed women continued to report elevated depression. SRI-exposed fetuses had smaller hippocampal volumes and reduced cortical gyrification, curvedness, and surface area. Subgroup analysis of stratification by EPDS scores revealed that SRI-exposed fetuses had reduced hippocampal volumes compared to unexposed fetuses with low and moderate, but not high, EPDS scores, and reduced cortical curvedness compared to unexposed subgroups. Among unexposed subgroups, fetuses exposed to high maternal EPDS scores had smaller hippocampal volumes compared to those with low scores. Placenta volume and microstructural diffusion were increased in the SRI-exposed compared to the unexposed group. Larger placental volume was associated with larger total fetal brain volume, and higher placental diffusion was associated with larger fetal white matter and cerebellar volumes in the SRI-exposed group. These findings suggest that prenatal SRI exposure may be associated with altered fetal hippocampal volumes, cerebral cortical maturation, and placental volume and microstructural diffusion. The clinical significance and long-term neurodevelopmental consequences of these structural alterations remain unknown and are currently under study.

title: Cortisol suppression impairs retrieval of emotional memory and changes its neural correlates immediately and four days post-treatment
abstract: Abstract Emotional memories are hard to forget. Yet, past research showed that very high and very low levels of the stress hormone cortisol crucially affect the retrieval of emotional memories both immediately and in a long-lasting manner. With a double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-subject fMRI design involving humans, the present study investigated the acute and lasting effects of cortisol suppression on the neural memory representations for emotional events. The pharmacological suppression of the physiological morning cortisol rise impaired immediate memory retrieval and disrupted the involvement of key brain regions, but also persistently altered the neural memory representations for these emotional memories, tested four days later. These results indicate that cortisol suppression distorts the engagement of the emotional memory neural network and is linked to lasting changes in emotional memory representations, suggesting potential for future research on clinical strategies for attenuating distressing emotional memories.
